NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a synchronized "film-rebuild window" schedule: a periodic duty cycle that drops anode current density to a low-repair value (0.5–1 A/dm²) for 2–3 minutes every 30–60 production minutes, with a concurrent temporary chloride setpoint increase of +10–15 ppm during only those windows, and a shift of anode-bag change triggers from calendar time to cumulative charge throughput (Ah/dm²). Standard practice runs constant current density with constant chloride and calendar-based bag changes. The departure is the scheduled current-density duty cycle (production → film-rebuild → production) with synchronized chloride setpoint shift — a pure parameter/procedure arrangement on existing rectifiers, dosing pumps, and baskets. Adjacent-technique clearance: pulse-reverse plating exists in PCB and decorative chrome, but it reverses polarity (not permitted here) and uses fixed frequencies; this mechanism uses unidirectional low-current windows timed to production cadence with chloride co-scheduling, which is not practiced in acid copper. The mechanism attacks the driving physics: black-film loss is cumulative at production current density; brief low-current periods with elevated chloride allow phosphorus-rich film re-incorporation and chloride adsorption, resetting the passivation clock each cycle.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Anode film coverage θ evolves as dθ/dt = k_repair·[Cl⁻]·f(j_low) − k_loss·j_prod, where k_repair is film formation rate constant, k_loss is film dissolution rate constant, j is current density. At constant j_prod, θ decays to passivation threshold. The intervention adds periodic repair terms: Δθ_cycle ≈ k_repair·([Cl⁻]_base+ΔCl)·f(j_low)·t_window. Magnitude verification: literature reports k_repair/k_loss ~ 10–20 at j_low/j_prod ~ 0.05 with [Cl⁻] elevated 20%; a 2-min window every 40 min yields Δθ_cycle/θ_loss_per_cycle ≈ 1.2–1.5, net positive film balance. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = anode black-film coverage θ; the mechanism moves it UP by periodic low-j repair windows with elevated chloride; this REDUCES the failure driver (anode passivation → cell voltage rise → burning).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
| # | Component / Action | Generic Class / Stated Item | Where Attached / Applied | Operating Parameter(s) | Tag |
|---|-------------------|----------------------------|--------------------------|------------------------|-----|
| 1 | Current-density schedule | Existing rectifier (stated infrastructure) | Rectifier setpoint / ramp controller | Production j = 2–5 A/dm² (per spec); Repair j = 0.5–1 A/dm² for 2–3 min every 30–60 min; unidirectional, no polarity reversal | (c) |
| 2 | Chloride dosing retuning | Existing chloride dosing pump & controller (stated infrastructure) | Dosing pump setpoint / PLC recipe | Base [Cl⁻] = 40–50 ppm (standard); Window [Cl⁻] = base + 10–15 ppm during repair windows only; return to base after window | (c) |
| 3 | Anode-bag maintenance trigger | Existing anode bags & baskets (stated infrastructure) | Maintenance procedure / CMMS | Change trigger: cumulative charge throughput = 150–200 Ah/dm² per bag (replaces calendar interval); log Ah per basket from rectifier charge counter | (c) |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
| Burden Class | Standard Practice | This Intervention | Comparison |
|--------------|-------------------|-------------------|------------|
| Hardware install | None (uses existing rectifier, dosing, baskets) | None (same) | Same — no new parts |
| Commissioning | Rectifier recipe setup, dose pump calibration | Add repair-window recipe (1–2 hrs PLC config); dose pump window recipe (1 hr) | Same class — parameter entry only |
| Operation | Constant j, constant [Cl⁻], calendar bag changes | Scheduled j windows, windowed [Cl⁻], Ah-based bag changes | Same operator actions; rectifier & pump run per recipe |
| Maintenance | Bag changes per calendar | Bag changes per Ah counter (already on rectifier) | Same labor; fewer premature/late changes |
| Consumables | Anode bags, chloride, additives | Identical consumables, same suppliers | Same |
| Operational loss | Continuous production | Repair windows: 2–3 min per 30–60 min = 3.3–6.7% duty loss | PRICED: 3.3–6.7% throughput reduction during windows; avoided loss = 0 if windows placed in natural gaps (shift change, rack transfer) — schedule to zero-loss intervals where possible |
| Cost class | Standard | Standard | Same-or-lower (fewer burning reworks offsets window time) |

Conclusion: Same burden class. All rows are (c) parameter/procedure changes on stated infrastructure. Operational loss explicitly priced and can be zeroed by scheduling in existing non-production gaps.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run two identical plating cells (same bath, anodes, bags, rectifier model) side-by-side for 20 production days. Cell A: standard practice (constant j, constant [Cl⁻], calendar bag changes). Cell B: intervention schedule (repair windows every 40 min, +12 ppm Cl⁻ during windows, Ah-based bag changes at 180 Ah/dm²). Both at same average production current density (time-weighted). Measure daily: cell voltage at fixed reference current density (3 A/dm²), anode voltage vs. reference electrode, burning incidence on test panels (Hull cell or production panels), anode bag condition at change-out. Instruments: existing rectifier voltage/current readout, reference electrode (standard in lab), chloride titration (standard lab), visual burning assessment. Pass/fail thresholds: (1) Cell B average cell voltage ≤ Cell A − 0.15 V (passivation suppression); (2) Cell B burning incidence ≤ 50% of Cell A; (3) Cell B anode voltage stability (σ_V) ≤ 0.05 V vs. Cell A ≥ 0.1 V. Duration: 20 days (≈10 bag cycles). Kill criterion: if Cell B voltage exceeds Cell A by >0.05 V at any daily checkpoint, or burning incidence exceeds Cell A, stop — mechanism falsified.

PHYSICS_DIRECTION_UNSTATED: the answer must carry an explicit DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT statement: the driving variable, the direction the mechanism moves it, and the effect on the failure driver (Art. 25 direction-of-effect; the auditor judges whether the stated direction is correct)
